title: Lessons from securing AI systems at runtime (agents, MCPs, LLMs)
shortSummary: A practical look at the security blind spots that emerge when AI agents and MCP servers are deployed in production. The authors found that hard problems arent model choice or prompt quality, they surface after deployment when agents call unmapped tools, LLMs access internal APIs through opaque chains, and execution identity diverges from user identity. They documented runtime visibility and governance solutions for these emerging threat patterns.
whyItMatters: As AI agents and MCP servers become critical control planes, traditional security assumptions break down. This post surfaces the operational gaps and offers a roadmap for runtime governance before they become incidents.

title: Kernel-enforced sandbox App and SDK for AI agents, MCP and LLM workloads
shortSummary: A new open-source kernel-enforced sandbox app and SDK designed to isolate AI agent, MCP server, and LLM workloads at the system level. By leveraging kernel-level enforcement rather than user-space restrictions, it provides stronger guarantees that agents cannot escalate privileges or exfiltrate data beyond their allocated sandbox.
whyItMatters: AI agents with broad system access are a growing attack surface. Kernel-level sandboxes provide a hardware-rooted trust boundary that cannot be bypassed by compromised agents, addressing one of the hardest problems in production AI deployment.

title: Launch HN: Freestyle – Sandboxes for Coding Agents
shortSummary: Freestyle is building a cloud platform purpose-built for coding agents, offering sandbox environments that behave like EC2 instances but with the ability to fork entire system memory horizontally in under 400ms. Unlike serverless deployments, these sandboxes let AI agents use the full power of a computer while sharing state across forks seamlessly.
whyItMatters: The next generation of AI agents needs more than serverless containers, they need full OS environments. Freestyles microsecond-memory-fork approach could unlock massively parallel agent workflows that were previously impossible on serverless infrastructure.

title: Show HN: Compose-to-Cloud Pulumi Providers for AWS, GCP, and Azure
shortSummary: Three free Pulumi providers (defang-aws, defang-gcp, defang-azure) that take a Docker Compose-like project specification and provision it as real cloud infrastructure, including VPCs, subnets, load balancers, serverless containers, managed PostgreSQL, Redis, and DNS. Move between clouds by changing a single import with no code changes.
whyItMatters: Multi-cloud and cloud-agnostic deployments remain painful. This tool lets teams define infrastructure once in Compose format and deploy to any major cloud, reducing vendor lock-in and operational complexity for AI and agent workloads.

title: AI coding agents accidentally introduced vulnerable dependencies
shortSummary: A developer discovered a cryptominer running on their Next.js server after an AI-assisted development workflow using Claude Code and OpenAI Codex accidentally pinned a vulnerable dependency version. The exploit chain was straightforward: AI-generated project with a vulnerable dependency allowed CVE-2025-29927 middleware bypass, leading to an automated scanner flagging it within hours and an attacker executing a miner download script.
whyItMatters: This is a cautionary tale about the security debt that vibe coding with AI agents introduces. When AI generates code faster than humans can audit it, vulnerabilities slip through. Automated security gates are now essential in AI-augmented development workflows.

title: Show HN: Tool to detect malware left behind after patching CVE-2025-55182
shortSummary: After a CVE-2025-55182 React Server Components RCE breach left crypto miners and persistence mechanisms on a patched server, the author built NeuroLint, a deterministic AST-based scanner that detects 80+ indicators of compromise including fake services, cron job persistence, suspicious processes, and mining configs. It works on Linux and Mac, takes about 5 minutes for a deep scan, and includes automated remediation.
whyItMatters: Patching a vulnerability does not remove existing infections. This tool addresses the gap between vulnerability remediation and actual host recovery, critical as CVEs like the React RCE see active exploitation in the wild.

title: I built sbsh: Persistent terminal sessions with discovery, profiles, and an API
shortSummary: sbsh provides persistent terminal sessions with built-in discovery, YAML-defined environment profiles for Kubernetes contexts and Terraform workspaces, multi-attach for shared debugging, and structured logging. It separates the terminal session from the supervisor so SSH sessions survive network drops, useful for long-running kubectl or Terraform sessions.
whyItMatters: DevOps workflows often involve long-running terminal sessions over unreliable connections. sbsh persistent searchable sessions with environment-aware profiles reduce human error when switching between dev staging and production Kubernetes clusters.

title: OpenCode – Open source AI coding agent
shortSummary: OpenCode is a fully open-source AI coding agent that has garnered over 1,200 points and 600+ comments on its launch. It provides an autonomous coding assistant that can read, write, and iterate on codebases without proprietary constraints, positioning itself as a transparent alternative to closed-source AI coding tools.
whyItMatters: Open-source AI coding tools are rare but increasingly demanded. OpenCodes traction signals strong interest in developer-controlled auditable AI coding agents, especially important given recent stories about AI-generated code introducing security vulnerabilities.

title: Lore – Open source version control system designed for scalability
shortSummary: Lore is an open-source version control system designed for massive scalability, competing with Git dominance. It launched with significant community interest earning over 1,200 points and 680 comments, suggesting developers are actively exploring alternatives to Git for large-scale repository management.
whyItMatters: Git architecture faces challenges at extreme scale. An open-source modern VCS could address performance and usability gaps that Git was not designed for, especially as AI-generated codebases grow larger and more complex.
